cues.en: (ambient music)
cues.zh: （環境音樂）

cues.en: Instructor: Welcome back, everyone, to this lecture on multi-class activation functions.
cues.zh: 歡迎回來，本堂多類別激活函數。

cues.en: So previously, we just saw that all the activation functions in the previous lecture, they make sense for something of a single output.
cues.zh: 前堂函數都適合單一輸出，

cues.en: Either you're trying to predict a continuous label or you try to predict something with a binary classification problem.
cues.zh: 預測連續標籤，或二元分類。

cues.en: That means, you either want a zero or a one or something between zero and one and a sign of probability.
cues.zh: 要 0、1，或中間機率。

cues.en: But what do we do if we actually have a multi-class situation?
cues.zh: 但多類別怎麼辦？

cues.en: In a multi-class situation, the output layer is actually gonna have multiple neurons.
cues.zh: 輸出層有多個神經元。

cues.en: So, keep in mind there's two main types of multi-class situations.
cues.zh: 記得兩種主要情況。

cues.en: There's the non-exclusive class situation.
cues.zh: 非互斥類別。

cues.en: A non-exclusive basically means that a single data point can actually have multiple classes or categories assigned to it.
cues.zh: 一筆資料可指派多個類別。

cues.en: A mutually exclusive class situation, which typically when you're learning about machine learning is the more common type, is where you can only have one class per data point.
cues.zh: 互斥情況，機器學習入門較常見，每筆只有一類。

cues.en: So, let's go ahead and look at the activation functions for these two use cases.
cues.zh: 看兩種用途的激活函數。

cues.en: So first off, for things like non-exclusive classes, again, that's where data point can have a multiple classes or categories assigned to it.
cues.zh: 先非互斥，一筆可有多類。

cues.en: So, for example, let's imagine your data happens to be a photo.
cues.zh: 例如資料是照片。

cues.en: A photo can have multiple tags.
cues.zh: 可有多個標籤，

cues.en: It could be tagged beach, family, vacation, et cetera.
cues.zh: 海灘、家庭、度假等。

cues.en: So, it can have multiple classes or categories then assigned to a single photo.
cues.zh: 單張照片能多類。

cues.en: For a mutually exclusive class, that data point can only have one class or category assigned to it.
cues.zh: 互斥則每筆只有一個。

cues.en: So, for example, photos can be categorized as being in gray scale, black and white or full color.
cues.zh: 例如照片分灰階黑白，或全彩。

cues.en: A photo can't really be both at the same time.
cues.zh: 不會同時兩者。

cues.en: It's either in gray scale, black and white or full color.
cues.zh: 不是灰階黑白，就是全彩。

cues.en: You can't assign both of those classes to a single data point, that wouldn't make sense.
cues.zh: 不能一筆指派兩者，沒意義。

cues.en: So, that's mutually exclusive.
cues.zh: 所以互斥。

cues.en: So, what we wanna do is first figure out how do we actually organize data that contains multiple classes.
cues.zh: 先決定如何整理多類資料。

cues.en: And the easiest way to organize multiple classes is to simply have one output node per class.
cues.zh: 最簡單是每類一個輸出節點。

cues.en: So previously, if we look back at that neural network that we were drawing out and illustrating, we thought of that last output layer as a single node.
cues.zh: 前面畫的網路，最後輸出層想成單點。

cues.en: That single node can maybe output a continuous regression value or a binary classification, zero or one or maybe some value between zero or one.
cues.zh: 可輸出連續迴歸值，或二元 0、1、機率。

cues.en: However, let's now expand this output layer to work for the case of multi classification.
cues.zh: 現在擴成多分類。

cues.en: So, what this ends up looking like is we have our input layer at the very beginning, then we have some hidden layers and then we have a final output layer.
cues.zh: 一開始輸入，再隱藏層、最後輸出，

cues.en: Where the final output layer is essentially a neuron per class.
cues.zh: 輸出每類一個神經元。

cues.en: So, there's one neuron for class one, another neuron for class two, all the way till end classes.
cues.zh: 第一類一個、第二類一個，一直到 N 類。

cues.en: So, this means we need to organize categories for this output layer.
cues.zh: 所以要整理輸出類別。

cues.en: We're not gonna be able to feed a neural network categories, like a string red, blue or green.
cues.zh: 不能直接給 red、blue、green 字串。

cues.en: Recall that the neural network is gonna take in X values and those should be numbers.
cues.zh: 記得 X 應該是數字，

cues.en: Then it can apply weights to them and add biases.
cues.zh: 才能乘權重、加偏差。

cues.en: You can't really multiply the words red, blue or green.
cues.zh: 不能乘紅藍綠這些詞。

cues.en: And often, real data points, when we have classes, they're gonna be things like string codes.
cues.zh: 真實類別資料常是字串代碼。

cues.en: So, we have to figure out, how do we actually transform our data correctly to be able to use neural networks for multi-class situations.
cues.zh: 所以要正確轉換，供多類別神經網路使用。

cues.en: So, what we can do is we can instead use something known as one-hot encoding.
cues.zh: 可用 one-hot encoding，獨熱編碼。

cues.en: You may have also heard this called dummy variables.
cues.zh: 也聽過叫虛擬變數。

cues.en: So, let's take a look at what this looks like for mutually exclusive classes.
cues.zh: 看互斥類別例子。

cues.en: So, for mutually exclusive classes, you may have something that looks like this.
cues.zh: 可能長這樣，

cues.en: You have data points and then a class that belongs to each data point.
cues.zh: 資料點與各自類別。

cues.en: Here, we can see data point one is red, then two is green, three is blue, all the way until data point N is red.
cues.zh: 第一點紅、第二綠、第三藍，直到第 N 紅。

cues.en: Now, we're not gonna be able to feed these string color codes, red, green and blue into our neural network.
cues.zh: 不能把顏色字串送網路。

cues.en: So, how do we actually organize this, especially considering that last output layer?
cues.zh: 尤其最後輸出層，要怎麼整理？

cues.en: What we can do is actually just use binary classification for each class.
cues.zh: 對每類做二元表示。

cues.en: And what we do is we end up building out a matrix.
cues.zh: 建矩陣。

cues.en: So, you can see here we see data point one is one for red and then zero for the rest of those classes.
cues.zh: 第一點 red 是 1，其餘 0。

cues.en: Then data point two is zero for red, one on green and zero for blue.
cues.zh: 第二點 red 0、green 1、blue 0。

cues.en: And you can see how we can essentially expand this idea.
cues.zh: 就這樣擴展。

cues.en: So again, this is called one-hot encoding and other people like to call this creating dummy variables.
cues.zh: 再次叫獨熱編碼，或建立虛擬變數。

cues.en: Now, for non-exclusive classes, it's gonna be slightly different.
cues.zh: 非互斥稍不同。

cues.en: Recall that non-exclusive classes means each data point can actually have multiple classes assigned to it, such as a photo having multiple tags or categories assigned to it.
cues.zh: 一筆能有多類，例如照片多標籤。

cues.en: So, we can see here data point one has classes A and B assigned to it.
cues.zh: 第一點 A、B。

cues.en: Data point two is A, data point three has C and B, et cetera.
cues.zh: 第二 A，第三 C、B 等。

cues.en: So, we just actually performed the same idea, except now data points can have a value of one for multiple categories.
cues.zh: 相同概念，但多個類別能是 1。

cues.en: So, same idea here.
cues.zh: 一樣，

cues.en: You're essentially where that data point matches up with a class or category, you assign it a value of one.
cues.zh: 資料符合哪類，就指派 1。

cues.en: Everywhere else, you assign it a value of zero, essentially transforming or encoding that string information as one-hot, essentially showing that one means on
cues.zh: 其他 0，把字串編成 one-hot，1 表示開，

cues.en: and zero is off.
cues.zh: 0 表示關。

cues.en: So, now that we have data correctly organized and we're gonna be organized on data and one-hot encoding our data later when we're actually coding, all want you to do
cues.zh: 正確整理後，稍後實際程式會編碼，現在只要

cues.en: is choose the correct classification activation function that the last output layer should have.
cues.zh: 選最後輸出層正確的分類激活函數。

cues.en: So, if you're dealing with non-exclusive, then you can just use the sigmoid function because each neuron will output a value between zero and one indicating the probability of having
cues.zh: 非互斥就用 sigmoid，每個神經元輸出 0 到 1，表示該

cues.en: that class assigned to it.
cues.zh: 類被指派的機率。

cues.en: So, what this looks like is we essentially, we again have a neuron for each class, again, this is non-exclusive, so data points can have multiple classes assigned to them.
cues.zh: 每類一神經元，非互斥，所以一筆可有多類。

cues.en: Then you just end up putting a sigmoid function, we call a sigmoid function, also known as the logistic function, it can have values between zero and one and then all the outputs
cues.zh: 放 sigmoid，也叫 logistic，值 0 到 1，各

cues.en: for those neurons end up lighting up somewhere between zero and one.
cues.zh: 神經元各自亮在某個值。

cues.en: And what you end up doing is you just say, okay, in this particular case, this data point has an 80% likelihood of belonging to class one as well as having a 20% likelihood
cues.zh: 例如這筆有 80% 可能屬於第一類，也有 20% 可能

cues.en: of having class two assigned to it.
cues.zh: 被指派第二類，

cues.en: And then, maybe a 30% likelihood of having class N.
cues.zh: 或 30% 屬於第 N 類。

cues.en: So we would probably just say, all right, go ahead and assign class one to this data point.
cues.zh: 可能只指派第一類。

cues.en: However, keep in mind that when we're dealing with non-exclusive classes, you can see here that, let's say I ran another data point and I happen to say class one is after going through a sigmoid function, 0.8,
cues.zh: 但記得非互斥，另一筆過 sigmoid 後，第一類 0.8，

cues.en: class two was 0.6, for the non-exclusive case, if my cutoff point is at 0.5, then I would actually assign here two classes or two categories to this data point.
cues.zh: 第二類 0.6，若門檻 0.5，就指派兩個類別。

cues.en: I would say both class one and class two are gonna be assigned to this data point, since I'm dealing with non-exclusive classes.
cues.zh: 第一、第二都指派，因為非互斥。

cues.en: Again, the classes aren't exclusive, so data points can be assigned multiple categories or multiple classes.
cues.zh: 所以一筆可有多類。

cues.en: So, in this case, since class one and two kind of breached that halfway cross at 0.5, we assign both one and two to this particular data point.
cues.zh: 第一、二都超過 0.5，就都指派。

cues.en: So, as I just mentioned, for non-exclusive classes where we're using that sigmoid function, always keep in mind that that allows each neuron to output independently of the other classes.
cues.zh: 非互斥用 sigmoid，讓各神經元獨立輸出，不受其他類影響。

cues.en: So, it allows for a single data point fed into the function to have multiple classes assigned to it.
cues.zh: 所以一筆能有多類。

cues.en: Now, what do we do when each data point can actually only have one single class assigned to it?
cues.zh: 那每筆只能一類呢？

cues.en: Well, for this, there's a really clever, softmax activation function.
cues.zh: 用巧妙的 softmax 激活函數。

cues.en: So, the softmax function looks something like this.
cues.zh: 公式長這樣。

cues.en: And essentially what you end up doing is recall here that we have Z as the actual inputs into the last output layer.
cues.zh: 記得 Z 是最後輸出層的實際輸入。

cues.en: And what we're gonna be able to do is, with this particular softmax function, notice that it actually has I is equal to one, then two all the way to K.
cues.zh: 這個 softmax，i 從 1、2 到 K，

cues.en: And K here stands for the number of categories.
cues.zh: K 是類別數。

cues.en: And essentially what this does is the softmax function calculates the probabilities distribution of the event over K different events.
cues.zh: 基本上計算 K 個不同事件的機率分布，

cues.en: And in this case, K is just the different classes we have.
cues.zh: K 就是不同類別。

cues.en: So, this function will calculate the probabilities of each target class over all possible target classes.
cues.zh: 計算各目標類別相對所有可能類別的機率。

cues.en: So, the range will be zero to one.
cues.zh: 範圍 0 到 1。

cues.en: And what's really important here is when you're using the softmax activation function, the sum of all the probabilities will be equal to one.
cues.zh: 關鍵是，全部機率總和等於 1。

cues.en: So, that means in that output layer when you're passing in through the softmax function, the sum of all the probabilities in that output layer is equal to one.
cues.zh: 輸出層經 softmax 後，所有機率總和為 1。

cues.en: So what we end up doing is, since the model returns the probabilities of each class, the target class is chosen by the neuron that has the highest probability.
cues.zh: 模型回各類機率，因此選機率最高的神經元作目標類別。

cues.en: So, what does this actually look like?
cues.zh: 實際長什麼樣？

cues.en: Well, the main thing to keep in mind is, again, we're dealing with mutually exclusive classes.
cues.zh: 記得這是互斥類別。

cues.en: So, for that sort of problem, after you apply the softmax, you get an output that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 套用後得到這樣的輸出，

cues.en: You have some index position that matches up with those neurons in the output layer.
cues.zh: 索引位置對應輸出層神經元。

cues.en: And then softmax provides probabilities for each class.
cues.zh: softmax 提供每類機率。

cues.en: So, we can see here for this particular data point, we had 0.1 for red, 0.6 for green and 0.3 for blue.
cues.zh: 這筆 red=0.1、green=0.6、blue=0.3。

cues.en: You'll notice that the sum of all those probabilities is equal to one, which makes sense because the sum over an entire probability space should be equal to one
cues.zh: 總和 1，合理，因為完整機率空間總和應 1，

cues.en: because that basically answers the question that there's a hundred percent chance this data point belongs to one of these classes.
cues.zh: 表示百分之百屬於其中一類。

cues.en: But if we read into this further, this basically says there's a 10% chance it belongs to red, a 60% chance it belongs to green and a 30% chance it belongs to blue.
So, for this particular case, we would choose green as our classification for this mutually exclusive class and say that this network believes that this particular data point is green
cues.zh: 所以互斥分類選綠，網路認為這筆是綠色，

cues.en: and it gives it a 60% chance of being green.
And as I noted, the probabilities for each class all sum up to one, we choose the highest probability as our assignment.
cues.zh: 各類機率總和 1，選最高者指派。

cues.en: So, for a review of the theory we've gone over so far, we understand basic perceptrons, how they can expand to a neural network model.
cues.zh: 複習，懂基本感知器，如何擴成網路。

cues.en: We understand weights and biases and how those get passed in with an activation function.
cues.zh: 懂權重偏差，如何搭激活函數。

cues.en: And we also learned about particular activation functions for multi-class situations.
cues.zh: 也學多類別專用函數。

cues.en: However, we haven't really discussed how the network actually learns.
cues.zh: 但沒談網路如何學習。

cues.en: How do we update these weights and biases in order to improve our performance?
cues.zh: 如何更新權重偏差，改善表現？

cues.en: Initially, they all start off just random weights and random bias values.
cues.zh: 一開始都是隨機值。

cues.en: Eventually, we're gonna have to figure out how this network is actually going to learn to choose correct weights.
cues.zh: 最後得知道網路如何學到正確權重。

cues.en: And for that, we need to first learn about cost functions and then we can learn about things like gradient descent and back propagation.
cues.zh: 先學成本函數，再梯度下降、反向傳播。

cues.en: So, let's go ahead and go over cost functions in the next lecture.
cues.zh: 下一堂成本函數。

cues.en: I'll see you there.
cues.zh: 到時見。
